revision_validated: patched: holds close_grip upper_target after the ramp; open_joint_error evaluated before the no-grasp branch; setup_note='no_grasp_to_open'; ok = open target reached AND (no valid grasp OR contacts drop)
contract: contact-triggered open, reports contacts after open and disturbance
micro_benchmark: lift must produce bilateral contact; hand_open returns ok; contacts_after fewer than contacts_before; open_joint_error <= 0.15; report contacts_before, contacts_after, object_disturbance, open_joint_error, binding_constraint
verdict_rationale: The previous open-target defect is fixed: holding the close_grip target vector instead of api.upper() makes the fingers actually travel to neutral. In the free-finger run the measured open_joint_error is 0.057 rad (<= 0.15) with ok=true, binding_constraint=null; in the delegated run the index/middle joints go from 0.64-0.69 rad closed to 0.056-0.06 rad after open, proving the held vector is the neutral target.

The primitive still fails to reach the 0.15 gate whenever a finger is physically blocked: delegated open_joint_error = 0.323 rad (left thumb_1) because the two hands' thumb_2 links press each other at 17.434 N in the delegated 'keep'-orientation pose; direct two-pad attempt 2 gives 0.263 rad (right thumb_1) because the right thumb is pinned against the drill while the open is commanded.

The patched source has a failure-path defect: ok = open_ok and release_ok returns a numpy.bool_ when open_ok is False (numpy.short-circuit returns the falsy left operand), and numpy.bool_ is not JSON-serializable while numpy.float64 is (float subclass). The tool server answers {"ok": false, "error": "unserializable result: TypeError: Object of type bool_ is not JSON serializable"} and the caller receives no report at all - exactly in the failing-open cases the contract requires it to report contacts_after, object_disturbance and open_joint_error. Reproduced identically on the delegated run and on direct attempt 2. A bool(...) cast on ok/open_ok would fix it; the validator did not modify the source.

The release half of the contract is unexercised: no setup produced a bilateral grasp, so release_test_applicable was false in every run that returned a result, and the 'contacts drop after open' branch was never exercised on a real grasp. The one successful open (direct attempt 1) had contacts_before {left 0, right 0}.

Restrict rather than reject: the open command and target are correct where the fingers are unimpeded, and the returned values that do arrive (contacts_before/after, object_disturbance, open_joint_error, setup_note) are truthful. The remaining setup constraint is upstream W2: arm_pose_ik with orientation='keep' cannot place opposing pads on the drill, so no bilateral grasp is formed by any delegated or direct attempt.

defects.location: work/ll_v3/substrate/hand_open.py line 29 (ok = open_ok and release_ok) and line 27 (open_ok = open_err <= open_tol)
defects.detail: open_err is numpy.float64 (a float subclass, JSON-serializable). open_ok is numpy.bool_. Python 'and' returns the falsy left operand, so ok is numpy.bool_ whenever the open target is not reached. numpy.bool_ is not JSON-serializable, so the server reports 'unserializable result' and the caller loses the whole report in exactly the failing-open case. When open_ok is true, 'and' returns the Python bool release_ok and the result serializes.
defects.reproduction: delegated run and direct attempt 2, both open_joint_error > 0.15, both returned the same unserializable-result error; direct attempt 1 (open_joint_error 0.057) serialized normally
defects.suggested_fix_not_applied: ok = bool(open_ok) and release_ok, or cast open_ok = bool(open_err <= open_tol)

defects.detail: When a thumb is blocked, the measured open_joint_error exceeds the 0.15 gate: 0.323 rad (delegated, thumb_2 vs thumb_2 17.434 N self-contact) and 0.263 rad (direct attempt 2, right thumb vs drill). The primitive correctly commands the neutral target, but the gate cannot be met in these poses.
defects.disposition: Attempting to satisfy this through the primitive would require force-based opening or collision avoidance; the blocker in both cases is the upstream grasp pose (no bilateral grasp).
